text: Welcome to week 12 of the official
NASCAR Gen 4 Cup Series. And this week,
you'll be finishing off the season at
the Kansas Speedway for 85 laps. You
probably know the drill for qualifying
this week. Use your first laps to get
the tires warm. Give the outside wall a
tap to calibrate your spatial awareness
and run around the top to build momentum
for your final lap. In the process, get
familiar with where your left front tire
sits when you run the bottom, as you
won't want to leave any room on the
table when the white flag flies. Run up
against the wall in turns three and four
and turn down the track as you take the
white flag.
Flying into turn one, you'll want to
turn the car into the corner, lift just
before the row of white lines, and let
the car roll until you get the left
front planted against the inside. He's
back onto the gas once the car hooks up,
but don't get all the way at it until
you can see the track begin to
straighten out. The car will shimmy up
the track on exit, so be ready for that.
Hit turns three and four with the same
energy. Lift and start rolling at the
white lines. Plant the car against the
bottom and ride the throttle as the car
begins the track out. Use the first and
second white lines as your references as
you slide up the track. Get back on the
gas and cut the apron to the finish.

Once the race begins, you'll be starting
confidently in second gear. There won't
be much wheel spin at the start, and
once you get a heat cycle or two in the
tires, you'll need to be careful. As you
get up to speed, make it your first
priority to position yourself as close
to the inside as possible through turns
one and two. The draft may play a factor
against the outside wall on the
straightaways, but as you'll see in a
few seconds, the best time through the
corners throughout the race will be the
bottom.
I ran 15 laps with times ranging from
30.4 to 30.8 seconds, and the outside
was clearly the winner. It's true that
you could maintain pace around the
outside using the seam as your
reference, but to do that, you would
need to maintain a higher midc corner
speed and place extra strain on your
right side tires. If these races end up
going green past the first 15 laps, that
extra wear would hit you like a truck.
So rather than flying by everybody on
the initial start, you might want to
hang out around the bottom and set a
comfortable pace. The car hooks up well
around the white line, so that could be
your ticket to the front.
With the fuel window of 46 to 50 laps,
taking four tires will probably be your
best bet. If the cautions fall in your
favor and put you in a position to make
it on one can or roughly 8.5 gallons of
fuel, you could justify taking right
sides only. But the circumstances need
to line up just right for that to work
out. You would need to be in the middle
of a green flag run. You would need a
comfortable lead or positioning close to
the leader before your stop. And you
would need certainty that the race would
continue to the end. Any other situation
in four tires would have you set. Keep
an eye on your fuel calculator as the
cautions fall and plan accordingly. You
may be able to pull one over the field
and with this being the final week of
the season would be a great way to go
out. If you can find your pace early in
the running, keep your right side tires
happy. Manage your strategy decisively,
you could end off the season with a win.
Good luck.
